messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Geographically Weighted Regression
parts:
My observation is because it fits n regressions each one using all the data. Even thou the weights are given by kernel functions, they sum more than one and each regression are independent. I personally prefer the use of spatially structured random effects for the coefficients. You may follow recent discussion in this list.
best,
Elias

messages.author: 68c425efdf6bd7f6
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Geographically Weighted Regression
parts: From my personal experience, I found Gwr partially quite unreliable. When compared to a Bayesian svc model, the coefficients vary much more and seem to be sometimes unrealistic. I also use a svc model rather than gwr. Also, keep in mind that gwr does not really model neighborhood, but creates an average within a circle.

Elias T. Krainski <eliask...@gmail.com> schrieb am So., 23. Dez. 2018, 02:23:
My observation is because it fits n regressions each one using all the data. Even thou the weights are given by kernel functions, they sum more than one and each regression are independent. I personally prefer the use of spatially structured random effects for the coefficients. You may follow recent discussion in this list.
best,
Elias

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Geographically Weighted Regression
parts:
However, you can use models that accounts for distance. For example, in INLA, you can consider a joint prior for the coefficients following a Matern covariance. There are examples in the spde book. Thus, you can even make a map (predict) of the coefficients and, additionally, build a significance map using the excursions package.
Elias
